small_guidance:
- The conv kernel dominates runtime; add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_OC (e.g. 64/128) paired with BLOCK_HW=32-64 and num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4 to better exploit C_OUT=64, and try tiling output spatial as 2D (BLOCK_OH × BLOCK_OW) so the kh/kw input rows stay contiguous and coalesced across the W dimension instead of using a flat hw range that crosses row boundaries.
- Cache weights once per (oc, ic) tile by hoisting the `tl.load(w_ptr + ...)` out of the kh/kw inner loops — load the full (BLOCK_OC, KH*KW) weight slab per ic and reuse across spatial tile; this cuts redundant weight loads by BLOCK_HW×.
- For gn_scale_maxpool_clamp, fuse the GN stats computation into the same kernel for small group sizes, or at minimum increase BLOCK_HW to cover the full H_OUT*W_OUT=1024 with one program per (N,C) using num_warps=4, removing the pid_hw axis entirely.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite conv2d as an explicit im2col-style GEMM with one program per (N, BLOCK_OC tile, BLOCK_OHW tile) and an inner K-loop over C_IN*KH*KW=72 using tl.dot on (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_K) × (BLOCK_K, BLOCK_HW) tiles. KH*KW*C_IN=72 is small enough that K can be a single tile; tl.dot on tensor cores will be far faster than the current scalar outer-product accumulation.
- Switch to a channels_last (NHWC) layout end-to-end so the C dimension is the contiguous axis for both conv weight loads and GN reductions; this also makes the maxpool reads contiguous along W.
- Fuse conv epilogue with GN+scale+maxpool+clamp by computing per-(N,group) statistics in a second pass that reads the conv output once, then a third kernel that re-reads conv output to apply norm+pool+clamp — or better, write conv output directly tiled by group so stats can be computed inline. Eliminate the separate gn_stats kernel launch.
